label: GO step after two consecutive unrewarded trials (losing streak)
explanation: Fires only at GO (100% of mass) and almost only when the previous trial was unrewarded (prev_reward==0 holds 98.6% of mass, recall 0.96; it never fires with reward input 1). But it is sparse within that set: only about 10% of GO-after-no-reward steps are active (precision 0.10). Requiring two unrewarded trials in a row raises precision to 0.29 (F1 0.39 dev, mass recall 0.65), and three in a row to 0.42, so the rate goes up with the length of the losing streak; in example windows the activation climbs over consecutive losses (e.g. 0.24, 0.52, 0.71, 0.76). Recorded predicate: two consecutive losses. All its variables are observed at GO. Other modulators: much more active early in the episode (rate falls steadily with ep_trial and is zero in trials 90-99, peaks around trial 2), more active when the previous choice was a1 or the episode started with S1 good, and active on switch trials (stay==0 lift 5x, though that is the upcoming choice of the agent). Mid-high value-head outputs are enriched. Never fires at D1 or D2, or after a rewarded trial. Precision stays incomplete, so the feature probably encodes a graded, episode-time-dependent signal of recent loss of reward, not a clean binary condition.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over last trial (GO: a1 S1 u, a1 S2 u, a2 S2 u) and trial before (GO: a1 S1 u, a1 S2 u, a2 S1 u); timing cues that raise it most: phase=GO & ep_dec=0, phase=GO & ep_dec=1, phase=GO & ep_dec=2.
